Exact options and behavior of the page cache. For a walkthrough, see [Cache server-rendered pages](/docs/dev/cache/pages).

## Route `cache` option

Accepted by `page()` and `index()` from `@vitnode/core/routing`.

| Name                   | Type     | Required | Default | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `maxAge`               | `number` | Yes      | -       | Seconds a stored page is fresh. Whole number from 1 to 31536000.             |
| `staleWhileRevalidate` | `number` | No       | `0`     | Extra seconds a stale page may be served while it re-renders. 0 to 31536000. |

`cache: false` declares that the route is not cached, which is also the default. The build fails with `invalid-cache` for a layout, an unknown key or a duration outside these ranges. A policy on an AdminCP route, an `/api` path or a route with `requires` (its own or a parent layout's) fails the build too.

## `vitNodeConfig.pageCache`

Set in `buildConfig()` in the host app's `src/vitnode.config.ts`.

| Name      | Type                               | Required | Default    | Description                                                                        |
| --------- | ---------------------------------- | -------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled` | `boolean`                          | No       | `true`     | `false` turns the cache off for every route. Development never caches either way.  |
| `storage` | `"memory" \| "redis"`              | No       | `"memory"` | `"redis"` reads `REDIS_URL` (and `REDIS_PASSWORD`, if set) when the server starts. |
| `routes`  | `Record<string, PageCacheSetting>` | No       | `{}`       | Per-route override, keyed by canonical path (`"/blog/:slug"`). `false` disables.   |

An override wins over the route's own `cache`, and may opt in one of the app's own route files. A key that matches no page route fails the build.

## `withPageCache(entry, options)`

From `@vitnode/core/tanstack/page-cache/server`. Wraps a TanStack Start server entry and returns one with the same `fetch`.

| Name      | Type                  | Required | Description                                     |
| --------- | --------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `buildId` | `string`              | Yes      | `pageCacheBuildId` from `src/page-cache.gen.ts` |
| `config`  | `VitNodeConfig`       | Yes      | The app's `vitNodeConfig`                       |
| `routes`  | `PageCacheRouteTable` | Yes      | `pageCacheRoutes` from `src/page-cache.gen.ts`  |

## Response headers

| Header            | Value                                 | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x-vitnode-cache` | `HIT`, `STALE`, `MISS`, `REVALIDATED` | Served from the cache, stale while refreshing, rendered and stored, or re-rendered after expiry |
| `x-vitnode-cache` | `BYPASS`                              | The request skipped the cache, or the render could not be shared                                |
| `cache-control`   | `no-cache`                            | A shared page: browsers and CDNs must revalidate with the `ETag`                                |
| `cache-control`   | `private, no-cache`                   | A shared page that also sets this visitor's locale cookie                                       |
| `cache-control`   | `private, no-store`                   | A page rendered for one visitor                                                                 |

Routes without a policy keep their usual headers and get no `x-vitnode-cache`.

## When a request skips the cache

A request on a cached route goes straight to the renderer when:

- its method is not `GET` or `HEAD` (`GET` and `HEAD` are cached separately);
- its query string has a parameter other than these analytics parameters, which are ignored: `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_term`, `utm_content`, `utm_id`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `gbraid`, `wbraid`, `dclid`, `msclkid`, `yclid`, `twclid`, `ttclid`, `li_fat_id`, `igshid`, `mc_cid`, `mc_eid`, `_ga`, `_gl`. A `?preview=` link is one such parameter;
- the locale rules redirect it, for example `/en/blog/x` to `/blog/x`;
- the server could not write an invalidation and has paused the cache.

Entries are keyed by the request origin (scheme, host and port), the path, the method and the build id. Each language's URL and each domain therefore has its own entry.

## Label and invalidate your own data

From `@vitnode/core/api/lib/page-cache`, for data a cached page reads from your own Hono routes.

| Function                                  | Returns                                | Behavior                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setPageCacheTags(c, tags)`               | `void`                                 | Labels the response. A cached page that reads it during its render is stored with these tags. |
| `invalidatePageCacheTags(tags, { mode })` | `Promise<PageCacheInvalidationResult>` | Invalidates every page stored with any of `tags`. `mode` is `"soft"` or `"hard"`.             |

```ts title="plugins/events/src/api/modules/events/routes/list.route.ts"
import { setPageCacheTags } from '@vitnode/core/api/lib/page-cache'

// in the handler, before returning the response
setPageCacheTags(c, ['events:list'])
```

```ts title="after the write commits"
import { invalidatePageCacheTags } from '@vitnode/core/api/lib/page-cache'

const result = await invalidatePageCacheTags(['events:list'], { mode: 'soft' })
if (result.status === 'failed') {
  await c.get('log').error('Cached event pages could not be invalidated.')
}
```

`status` is `"done"`, `"failed"` (with `error`) or `"not-configured"` when this process has no page cache, such as an API server without `pageCache` in `buildApiConfig`. Content Engine routes and writes already do this for you.

## `buildApiConfig({ pageCache })`

Only for an API that runs in its own process next to a web app using `storage: "redis"`.

| Name          | Type      | Required | Default | Description                                                              |
| ------------- | --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `storage`     | `"redis"` | Yes      | -       | Writes invalidations through the API's `redis` client, or `REDIS_URL`.   |
| `maxLifetime` | `number`  | No       | `86400` | Longest `maxAge + staleWhileRevalidate` of any cached route, in seconds. |
